relevance_note: Case series of four Chinese patients with Blau syndrome and NOD2 variants, each described individually (e.g. "A heterozygous R334W variant in the NOD2 gene was identified and the diagnosis of BS was confirmed").
method_note: Read the paper directly; a short script assembled the JSON and built the Table 1 spans from the table rows (Table 1 has patients as columns under the header '| Patients | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |'); spans were checked verbatim by script. Labels 'Patient 1'-'Patient 4' follow the text's own labels. Patient 2 is the son of Patient 1. Table 1 '+' cells were used as supporting spans for observed features; '–' cells are not defined as absent in the table notes, so they were not used to exclude anything (Patient 2 eye/fever and Patient 4 fever exclusions come from the text; Patient 3 fever and Patient 4 skin are not reported from the table). Literature review of 62 patients (38 publications) gives only counts, so no rows. The previously reported '13-year-old Chinese boy with refractory BS' treated with tocilizumab [7] was given a row ('ref [7] patient') because sex and age are stated; no NOD2 variant is printed for him, so no variant row. 'three patients we have reported before [8]' does not say which three patients, so source_reference_in_review was left 'not reported' for Patients 1-4. Patient 4: the paper says 'A de novo heterozygous R334Q variant' but reports no parental testing, so inheritance is 'not reported' (rule 8). Patient 2: inheritance 'inherited maternal' because his mother (Patient 1) is stated to carry heterozygous R334W; Patient 2's own zygosity is not stated. Fig. 2 legend: 'WBC, ESR, and CRP remained normal in all except patient 3' at the 18-month visit (after IFX); recorded as excluded 'elevated ESR and CRP' rows for Patients 1, 2 and 4 with that timing, but the checklist item 'elevated inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP)' was left 'not reported' for them because this is a post-treatment state and the baseline status is not stated (Table 1 gives values without reference ranges). Possible tension: the Discussion says Patient 2 at diagnosis 'had only arthritis without uveitis and joint deformities', whereas the case text reports papules from 6 months and camptodactyly that 'gradually developed'; treated as time-qualified, camptodactyly kept observed. Patient 3 'without obvious deformity' recorded as excluded deformity; camptodactyly left not reported. Patient 4 'interphalangeal joint flexion' not mapped to camptodactyly (paper does not use that word). Patient 4 'no dermatitis' excludes dermatitis only; the composite checklist item 'granulomatous dermatitis or skin rash' left not reported. Ages at presentation (32, 8, 36, 25 years) equal Table 1 'Age at diagnosis' and are recorded only there; age at last evaluation not stated for Patients 1-4.
